title: Hosted API Lite Slate: PRD, Scope Clarification, Acceptance Criteria & Launch Checklist
creator: Ava Nguyen
description: Purpose: Define a minimal, interoperable PRD for a 'Lite Slate' of hosted inference endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) targeted at rapid onboarding for small/medium customers while preserving safety, observability, and predictable economics. This document clarifies requirements, enumerates scope changes vs. full-surface PRDs, and provides a concrete launch checklist with acceptance criteria and rollback gates.
scope_in:
- Expose compact endpoint contracts for: chat (conversational API), completions (single-shot generation), embeddings (vector encode), and rerank (similarity-based reranking).
- Streaming support for chat & completions (text-only).
- Basic tenant isolation (per-tenant API keys, usage accounting).
- Runtime defaults tuned for cost-effectiveness (presets for batching/quantization).
- Minimal observability: per-endpoint latency, error rate, token cost telemetry, and canary dashboards.
- Safety guardrails: prompt-safety filters and basic rate limits.
scope_out:
- No multi-protocol surface (gRPC/other) or advanced composable endpoints.
- No multi-model orchestration (mosaic routing) in initial lite slate.
- No tenant-managed private deployment package; this is hosted-only.
- No advanced KV cache controls surfaced to customers (runtime-managed only).
- No long-term retention analytics beyond 30d for the initial rollout.
requirements: Functional: Provide REST endpoints: /v1/lite/chat, /v1/lite/completions, /v1/lite/embeddings, /v1/lite/rerank with consistent authentication headers and JSON schemas.
Behavioral: Deterministic contract for input/output fields; stable schemas for customer SDKs during launch window.
Rate limits: Default per-account QPS and token caps, with simple upgrade path to higher tiers.
Defaults: Endpoint presets for latency (low-latency), cost (economy), and balanced. Customers can override via documented 'profile' parameter but not arbitrary runtime knobs.
Billing: Usage metering per token for chat/completions, per-vector for embeddings, and per-request for rerank. Integrate with existing billing pipeline.
Safety: Integrate hosted prompt-safety service; block high-risk content according to current policy version. Expose a 403 code for safety blocks with a reference code in response.
Docs: Quickstart, SDK snippet, schema examples, migration notes from existing endpoints (if any).
non_functional_requirements: Latency: p95 <= 220ms for embeddings; p95 <= 400ms for short-completion (<=128 tokens); chat streaming first-byte <= 180ms for 90% of requests in supported regions.
Availability: 99.9% monthly uptime SLA for lite slate endpoints in hosted region(s).
Scalability: Autoscaling to absorb 3x baseline traffic burst without errors; throttling behavior documented.
Cost profile: Unit cost targets to be within 12% of comparable 'economy' presets from platform benchmarks.
Observability: Canary dashboard with per-route latency/error/token cost, traces linked to request-id, alerting for degradation.
Security: TLS everywhere, KMS-backed service keys for internal signing, and audit logging of admin actions.
Compliance: Initial rollout in non-EU regions; EU rollout gated on data residency clarifications and DPA updates.
acceptance_criteria: API contract: All four endpoints implement the documented request and response schemas with example fixtures in the repo.
SDK tests: Official JS and Python SDK integration tests pass against a staging stack and are included in CI.
Performance: Benchmarks meeting NFR latency targets in staging under synthetic traffic (see bench artifacts link).
Reliability: Canary run for 72 hours with error rate <= 0.5% and no sustained latency regression >20% vs baseline.
Safety: Prompt-safety integration active; at least one block example tested and an error code returned as specified.
Billing: Usage events for these endpoints flow through billing pipeline end-to-end and invoices reflect test usage in sandbox accounts.
Docs & Guides: Quickstart, migration notes, and troubleshooting guide published in Confluence/Docs with review approval from Developer Experience.
Operational Runbook: On-call playbook, rollback plan, and escalation matrix documented and linked to pager duty schedules.
Security Review: Completed and signed off by security with required mitigations tracked as issues.
Launch Signoff: Cross-functional signoff (PM, Eng, DX, Security, SRE) recorded in the release ticket before cutover.
Region gating: EU/UK rollout gating tasks created; initial global rollout excludes EU until gating closed.
rollout_plan: Alpha: Internal alpha with 3 partner accounts in staging (2w).
Canary: 5% traffic to lite-slates in us-west for 72h with active monitoring and rollback gate (2w).
Gradual: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 4 weeks with automated traffic ramp if canary metrics stable.
Documentation: Publish quickstart & migration docs at canary start.
Billing: Enable billing in parallel for canary tenants; verify metering.
launch_checklist: API schemas stable and published to the openapi registry.
Canary dashboard configured with alert thresholds (latency, errors, cost delta).
Safety enforcement rules deployed and tested with deterministic inputs.
On-call runbook and rollback steps posted to Confluence.
Security review completed and findings remediated or accepted.
Legal/compliance: DPA check for EU customers and data residency note included.
Support readiness: Tier-1 playbook and response templates available.
Feature flags in place for instant cutover/roll-back.
Marketing: Launch-notification draft to Sales/Partners for selective early access.

notes: This lite slate is intentionally opinionated: predictable defaults, reduced knobs, and focused observability make it suitable as an entry point for customers who prioritize rapid onboarding and cost predictability. Post-launch roadmap will expand to multi-region parity, tenant-configurable caching policies, and extended telemetry retention.
